text: Boavita is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, within the Northern Boyacá Province subregion. Its urban center lies in the Eastern Ranges of the Colombian Andes at an elevation of 2,114 metres (6,936 ft), approximately 184 kilometres (114 mi) from Tunja, the department's capital. The municipality shares borders with Capitanejo, Santander, and the Nevado River to the north, San Mateo and La Uvita to the east, Tipacoque and Soatá to the west, and Susacón to the south. The name Boavita originates from the Chibcha language and does not mean "good life"; instead, it signifies "Point on the hill worshipping the Sun" or "Gate of the Sun." Before the Spanish conquest, the area was inhabited by a tribe known as the Guavitas, part of the Laches and Muisca groups, and was governed by a cacique who remained loyal to the Tundama of Tundama. Modern Boavita was officially founded on February 9, 1613, by Sr. Hugarte. The primary economic activities in the municipality are agriculture, livestock farming, and mining, with key agricultural products including dates, sugarcane, yuca, coffee, cotton, potatoes, maize, chick peas, beans, peas, wheat, and arracacha. Mining in the region involves carbon extraction. Boavita experiences a subtropical highland climate (Köppen classification: Cfb), characterized by moderate temperatures year-round. Its geographic coordinates are 6°20′N 72°35′W (6.333°N 72.583°W).
